newsitem.title: INDIA: India depository sales on first in, first out basis.
newsitem.headline: India depository sales on first in, first out basis.

text.p: Sales of shares on India's National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) will be executed on a "first in, first out" basis, NSDL's managing director told Reuters on Thursday.
C.B. Bhave said if a client dematerialised say two lots of shares of any given company at different times, he would have to sell the first group of shares before he sold the second.
"So if I had first dematerialised a particular lot of 100 shares then the first sale of 100 that I make will be taken to be that first lot," Bhave said.

Dematerialisation is the process by which the physical certificates of an investor are taken back by the company or registrar and destroyed. An equal number of of securities are credited to the electronic holdings of the investor.
Bhave said the client would always hold a record of when he bought each particular lot of shares.
"What he would not have after dematerialisation is exactly when did he sell them.. the loss is that in the depository these shares will be treated as first in, first out," Bhave said.
NSDL -- the country's first share depository -- is scheduled to be launched on Friday.
